Added `_append_deprecated_label` in `src/click/core.py`. Commands and options with empty or missing help now render just `(DEPRECATED)` with no leading space.
The check passes (722 passed), though I added no test for the empty-help case.

Fixed `write_usage` in `src/click/formatting.py`. With no `args` it now writes `Usage: cli\n` (checked by calling it directly) instead of a blank line.
`tests/test_formatting.py` passes, 27 tests, but it already passed before my edit and has no test for the empty-args case, so the fix is only confirmed by that direct call.

Added `Option.make_metavar` in `src/click/core.py`. With `show_choices=False` and no explicit `metavar`, `--help` now shows `CHOICE` (the type name) instead of `[a|b]`.
`tests/test_options.py` passes (113 passed), and a manual `--help` run showed `-g CHOICE` for the hidden-choices option and `-h2 [a|b]` for the default one.

Short help now skips a period when the next word starts in lowercase, so `vs.` and `e.g.` no longer end it. The change is in `src/click/utils.py:92`, and the check fails 2 of 14 (12 pass).

The 2 failures are the `sentence < max` cases (`123 567 9. aaaa bbb`). That test expects a sentence end before a lowercase `aaaa`, which contradicts the new rule, and I can only edit `src/click/**`, so I left it. Do you want that test changed to an uppercase next word, such as `9. Aaaa bbb`?

`prompt()` with `hide_input=True` now shows the type's own error message, with the entered value masked as `********`. The change is in `src/click/termui.py`. The check passes (204 passed, 4 skipped), and a manual run printed `Error: ******** is not a valid integer.`

The check passed (664 tests in `tests/test_options.py`), but I added no tests for these two cases, and the quoted format is my guess at the intended wording.

Error hint now joins all non-shadowed help names (e.g. `-h/--help`) via `get_help_option_names` in `src/click/exceptions.py`. I also made that method keep the configured order instead of going through a set, in `src/click/core.py`.
`tests/test_formatting.py`: 17 passed. I didn't add a test for the shadowed `-h` case, and I didn't run the rest of the suite.
